notes: docs/theory/paper_b_prior_art_and_names.md. Software, v1.0, 4 July 2026, MIT. Run first-hand and compared against the laboratory's counts; not read about. Computes four of the Paper B cluster's objects: the survivor recursion W[k][d] = W[k-1][d] + W[k-1][d-1] under LAMBDA = log2 3, the survivor count N_d (his D_Unconverged), the minimal certificate count M_d (his B_Converged, zero exactly at our free lengths), and the odd-count refinement word_counts(d)[o] (his Counting by Hamming Weight, W[d][u], identical to ours for d = 1..22). Also prints the minimal certificate length as Glide, on the accelerated-map convention (Glide(27) = 59, not the standard map's 96). Guarded by tests/research/juggler_sequence/test_collatz_bridge.py. IT COMPUTES AND DOES NOT PROVE: both manuals are seven-page installation guides with no mathematics. His three papers have their own records (hikawa-nakanishi-2026-parity-vector-analysis, hikawa-2026-finite-dimensional-parity-vectors, hikawa-2026-finite-parity-vector-structures) and all three are unread here; this toolkit is a declared supplement to the first two.
title: Collatz Parity Vector Toolkit, version 1.0
